revisionDesc.change: Vote - AcceptText - See comments by Gonis and Fournet.

General - I have already published this correction in Jean-Luc Fournet, « Sur les premiers documents juridiques coptes (2) : Les archives de Phoibammôn et de Kollouthos », Études coptes XIV, Seizième journée d’études (Genève, 19-21 juin 2013), (Cahiers de la Bibliothèque copte 21), Paris 2016, p. 119,n. 31. I propose to read: Α̣ὐ̣ρηλία Τσῦρ̣ος. L. 29, instead of Τσυρα, there is Τσύρου.

Vote - AcceptText - Α[ὐ]ρ̣ηλία looks good, but Τσυ[ρ]α̣ς is very difficult, as the letter before sigma cannot be alpha (omicron much easier but I agree it's not υ̣ἱός). Τσ could also be dotted. Settle for Α[ὐ]ρ̣ηλία Τσυ[.1]ο̣ς?

Submit - In ed. princ. the name of the seller in line 14 was read Τιρηνατ ὑ̣ιὸς Φοιβάμμων, even though the ἡ προκ(), the subscriptions of the witnesses referring to the female seller by the phrase ἀκούσας παρὰ τῆς θεμένης, and the mention of the name Tsyra in l. 29 indicate a female party. The reading was later improved by James Keenan who proposed the reading Ⲧ̣ⲥ̣ⲩ̣ⲣ̣ⲁ̣ Ⲥⲁⲃ̣ⲓⲛⲟⲥ ϥⲟⲓⲃⲁⲙⲟⲛ (BL 10: 282). Ι propose the simpler reading: ⳨ Α[ὐ]ρ̣ηλία Τσυ[ρ]α̣ς Φοιβάμμων in which only the alpha in Τσυ[ρ]α̣ς is problematic, but we may assume that the upper stroke ascending from the lacuna belonged to the upper curved stroke of alpha and the trace below was the lower part of the same letter.

Commit - In ed. princ. the name of the seller in line 14 was read Τιρηνατ ὑ̣ιὸς Φοιβάμμων, even though the ἡ προκ(), the subscriptions of the witnesses referring to the female seller by the phrase ἀκούσας παρὰ τῆς θεμένης, and the mention of the name Tsyra in l. 29 indicate a female party. The reading was later improved by James Keenan who proposed the reading Τ̣σ̣υ̣ρ̣α Σα̣βίνος Φοιβάμμων (BL 10: 282). We, however, propose the simpler reading: ⳨ Α[ὐ]ρ̣ηλία Τσυ[ρ]α̣ς Φοιβάμμων in which only the alpha in Τσυ[ρ]α̣ς is problematic, but we may assume that the upper stroke ascending from the lacuna belonged to the upper curved stroke of alpha and the trace below was the lower part of the same letter. The rest of the letters do not even need dots.
